title: image scp: expose mapping-aware, reflink-backed local image transfer
body:
### Feature request description

Expose an efficient, mapping-aware local image-transfer backend through `podman image scp`, allowing transfers between independent rootless and rootful stores to use reflinks where the backing filesystem supports them.

The desired workflow is to reuse an image already present in one local store without downloading it again or serialising all file contents through an archive when a compatible local fast path is available. Source and destination stores should remain independent, with correct destination UID/GID mappings and filesystem metadata.

### Suggest potential solution

Integrate the splitfdstream infrastructure introduced in [container-libs#651](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/651), which separates layer metadata from file content and passes file contents as file descriptors, into the same-host `podman image scp` path.

Requested properties:

- Access source content in the appropriate source-user context; translate ownership and other metadata for the destination store rather than cloning a writable store or its database.
- Reuse file extents through reflinks when source and destination permit it, without coupling their subsequent modifications.
- Preserve image identity and validate the transferred content.
- Document fast-path capability detection and fallback behaviour when reflinks or the required backend are unavailable.

This is a request for CLI integration of that infrastructure, not a claim that the merged library work already provides this complete rootless/rootful workflow.

### Have you considered any alternatives?

The documented `podman image scp` command already supports same-host transfers between rootful and rootless storage; its documented archive formats provide a transfer route. `podman save` and `podman load` are another local-transfer option that avoids registry downloads.

A raw `cp --reflink=auto` clone is not an equivalent image import: sharing file extents does not itself translate UID/GID mappings or reconcile namespace-dependent storage/database state.

### Additional context

The usefulness of efficient rootful/rootless image sharing was already discussed in [container-libs#651](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/651#issuecomment-5956922112).

[`podman image scp` documentation](https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-image-scp.1.html).

A motivating use case is a rootless image build followed by a privileged disk-image bake, with both independent stores on the same btrfs filesystem.
